column3: The subject form of a pronoun before 가 (내가, 제가, 네가, 누가).
The subject forms back to the plain pronoun, before a particle that is no subject (나를).

A passive verb that no Korean passive word reads yet, with a person before に as its agent an object of を in its clause and no subject or topic (が, は, も, って) before the に, is the act of that person: the に is the subject (이)가, with a pronoun in its subject form, and the verb is active (弟に手紙を破られた 남동생이 편지를 찢었다, 俺に頭を撫でられる 내가 머리를 쓰다듬는다). Not without an object (母に叱られた 어머니에게 야단맞았다), nor when the verb describes a noun after it that is no noun.clause (彼女に別れ話を切り出された情けないヤツ keeps the passive) or another verb that is no auxiliary of its て form follows it in the sentence (吸われ、自らも吸血鬼化した keeps the passive).

column3: The してもら read 받다 (지도를 받다, 설명받다) is 해 주다 when a person before it, with に read 에게 and no other に, no は, が or から, no verb but an adjective in く and no punctuation between, does it for the speaker, with no subject or topic (が, は, も, って) before the person in the clause: the giver then becomes the subject (benefactive-provider). Not right after a verbal noun of noun.receive-verbal, whose 받다 is one Korean verb (紹介してもらった 소개받았다). After an adverb, an adjective in く or a verb in ように with no object を before it, it is 해 주다 too (優しくしてもらった 다정하게 해 주었다), but not after よく (잘 대접받다). A もら read 달라고 하다 (a request) after a causative is the plain 주다: the causative asks leave, not a favour (見極めさせてもらおう).

column3: The copula after a habitual past read in 곤 했 (놀곤 했다, 놀곤 했어).

A past verb with ものだ or もんだ at the end of a sentence (or before だが), with no negative, after a word of adverb.habitual in its clause (no other verb between, but for the verb of a ていた), is what one used to do: 곤 했다, the copula taking the ending (毎日遊んだものだ 매일 놀곤 했다). よく does so too, as 자주, unless it opens the sentence or a quote, a comma or も follows it, a quoting と goes before it (とはよく言ったものだ) or the copula wonders (だな, だね, だわ: よく了承したものだな). Not when a topic in は before it is neither a person nor a time (この本は毎日読んだものだ 매일 읽은 것이다).

column3: A ば or たら condition read (으)면 before a main clause in the past is one that did not hold, (았)더라면: a condition of ている or of ない (an adjective or いない, not the copula でなければ) in ば before a sentence that ends in the past (降っていなければ 오지 않았더라면, 君がいなければ 네가 없었더라면), and any ば or たら before a sentence that ends in a past with のに, かもしれない, だろう or はず (来れば間に合ったのに 왔더라면, 違っていたら刺さっていたかもしれない), unless the condition is one of seeing, saying or thinking (傍から見れば). A verb negated in ば (来なければ) takes it only before a sentence that ends in a past negative, a past of いい or such a supposition (来なければ乗ることもなかった 오지 않았더라면), not before a plain past of what followed (開けなければ並んだ). A quote (と, って), a clause that ends in a comma and no condition, or the end of the sentence stops the search, so a condition inside what is thought keeps (으)면; so do an obligation (なければならない) and a condition after と (としたら) or before a list in も (もいなければ).
